title: D1-1a-R4: Robust Membrane-Area Feasibility — Design Feasibility Check
question_prompt:
D1-1a-R4: Robust Membrane-Area Feasibility — Design Feasibility Check

An SWRO project has already procured the high-pressure pump and membrane elements, but during detailed design the owner increases the minimum production requirement and tightens the permeate-salinity limit. Because the major equipment is fixed, Feed pressure, A_comp, and B_comp cannot be changed; the engineering team can only vary total effective membrane area. Use simulate_ro across the three design-feed cases to determine whether any membrane-area range can simultaneously satisfy production, Recovery, Flux, Salt rejection, and permeate-NaCl requirements. The correct conclusion may be “no robust feasible area.” If no common interval exists, locate the production-driven area boundary and the water-quality/operational area boundary separately and prove the conflict numerically rather than forcing a recommendation.

Fixed model and equipment parameters | Three design cases
Parameter | Value | Unit | Notes | Case | NaCl mass fraction | Temperature °C
Feed mass flow | 4.3 | kg/s | Same for all three cases | A Normal | 0.031 | 30
Feed pressure | 51 | bar | High-pressure pump setting is fixed and cannot be adjusted | B High salinity | 0.035 | 23
A_comp | 4e-12 | m/s/Pa | Membrane type is fixed | C High temperature | 0.031 | 38
B_comp | 4.2e-08 | m/s | Membrane type is fixed
Permeate pressure | 1.013 | bar | Fixed | Common design constraints
Pressure drop | 0.653 | bar | Fixed | Metric | Requirement | Notes
Channel height | 0.002 | m | Fixed | Permeate production | ≥ 5.15 m³/h | Must be met in all three cases
Spacer porosity | 0.75 | - | Fixed | Recovery | ≤ 48.0% | Benchmark constraint
Module length | 20 | m | Fixed | Flux | ≤ 18.0 LMH | Benchmark constraint
CP / mass transfer | calculated | - | Use WaterTAP calculated option for both | Salt rejection | ≥ 98.65% | Benchmark constraint
Permeate NaCl | ≤ 475 mg/L | Benchmark constraint

Task requirements: use multi-round tool reasoning to assess robust feasibility of one common membrane area across multiple operating cases
1. E1 — Identify this as a robust membrane-area feasibility-window problem. Area is the only design variable; do not assume that larger area is always safer.
2. E2 — Start from a reasonable initial area (400 m² is suggested), simulate at least one design case, and correctly interpret Qp, Recovery, Flux, Rejection, and NaCl.
3. E3 — Screen A/B/C at the same initial area to identify the currently most limiting case and constraint. Then prioritize the boundary with the highest information gain rather than brute-forcing every area × case combination.
4. E4 — Lower boundary / production requirement: use multiple simulate_ro calls to locate the integer-area transition from insufficient production to the first point satisfying the relevant constraints, with 1 m² resolution.
5. E4 — Upper boundary / conflict search: continue varying area and actively check whether Recovery, Flux, Rejection, or NaCl develops a new failure. Do not assume the upper boundary is controlled by the same metric as in another item.
6. E4 — Robust verification: if a feasible set exists, recheck its boundary points and the final recommended area under A/B/C. If the feasible set is empty, provide sufficient boundary evidence to prove there is no overlap.
7. Final recommendation rule: if a robust integer feasible window exists, choose the area that maximizes the minimum distance to the first failing boundary on either side; if tied, choose the smaller area. If the window is empty, report “no feasible area” and do not recommend an Area.
reference_answer:
D1-1a-R4: Gold Answer — Constraint Conflict and Empty Feasible Window

Reference efficient trajectory: screen A/B/C at 400 m² and identify the water-quality risk; move toward smaller areas to confirm that water quality improves while production falls; use 308→309 m² to determine the maximum area allowed by water quality and 354→355 m² to determine the minimum area required by production. The intervals do not overlap, so stop and report no feasible Area.

Lower-bound production evidence: Case B production boundary — 354 m² = 5.142 m³/h (fail), 355 m² = 5.150 m³/h (pass)

dimensions.evaluation_focus: Use the correct tool and avoid irrelevant calls
dimensions.full_credit: Primarily use simulate_ro; each call directly serves the current boundary or verification question
dimensions.case_observation: No cost/chemistry tools are needed; RO performance simulation is sufficient

dimensions.dimension_label: E2 Information gain and call ordering
dimensions.full_credit: First screen cases at a common Area, then refine the most likely controlling boundary
dimensions.medium_credit: Ordering is mostly reasonable but includes low-information points
dimensions.case_observation: Case screening → bracketing → 1 m² boundary confirmation

dimensions.evaluation_focus: Make the next call depend on observations
dimensions.full_credit: Pass/fail and newly emerging limiting mechanisms directly determine the next Area/Case
dimensions.low_credit: Uses a preset fixed sequence and ignores observations
dimensions.case_observation: Pay special attention to lower and upper boundaries being controlled by different cases/constraints

dimensions.evaluation_focus: Obtain sufficient evidence within a reasonable call budget
